record.original_question: Let v1, ..., vn be a linear ordering of the vertices of a graph G, and for each vertex vi define d-(vi) = |{j < i : vivj in E(G)}| and d+(vi) = |{j > i : vivj in E(G)}|. A Type-A order is one in which every vertex v satisfies that d-(v) is odd or 0. Can it be decided in polynomial time whether a graph G admits a Type-A order or a Type-B order, where a Type-B order requires that each vertex either has d-(v) odd or 0, or else has d-(v) even and d+(v) = 0?

evidence.quote: Suppose that the vertices of a graph G are put in a linear order v1, . . . , vn. For i = 1, . . . , n define d-(vi) = |{j < i: vivj in E(G)}| and d+(vi) = |{j > i: vivj in E(G)}|.
Type-A order: for each v in V (G), d-(v) is odd or equal to 0; Type-B order: for each v in V (G), d-(v) is odd or equal to 0 (as in a Type-A order), or d-(v) is even and d+(v) = 0.
Problem 7.1 Can it be decided in polynomial time whether a graph G admits a Type-A order, or a Type-B order?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple graph on n vertices. Given a linear ordering v_1, v_2, …, v_n of V, define for each vertex v_i:
  d^-(v_i) = |{ j < i : v_i v_j ∈ E(G) }|,
  d^+(v_i) = |{ j > i : v_i v_j ∈ E(G) }|.

Call such an ordering a Type-A order if every vertex v satisfies
  d^-(v) is odd, or d^-(v) = 0.

Call it a Type-B order if every vertex v satisfies one of:
  (i) d^-(v) is odd, or d^-(v) = 0; or
  (ii) d^-(v) is even and d^+(v) = 0.

Question: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given an input graph G, decides whether G admits a Type-A order? Is there a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether G admits a Type-B order?
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of the recognition complexity for Type-A or Type-B orders in this sense was found through web search; the question is posed as an open problem and no follow-up establishing polynomial-time algorithms or hardness was located.
